ui.about.title: About QuEst
ui.about.cite: If you use QuEst in a scientific publication, please cite:
ui.help.title: QuEst — help
ui.help.text:
# QuEst — transient decay of a tethered dye

Predicts the fluorescence decay of a dye on a flexible linker from the
structure alone: the dye diffuses inside its accessible volume, is quenched on
contact with nearby amino acids (PET), and — with FRET enabled — transfers to
an acceptor.

## What to set
1. **Structure** — a PDB/CIF file or a four-character RCSB ID, and the residue
   the dye is attached to.
2. **Dye** — linker length, width and dye radius define the accessible volume.
3. **Simulation** — the unquenched lifetime, the diffusion coefficient and how
   long to simulate. `t_step` must resolve the fastest motion; the defaults are
   measured, not guessed.
4. **Quenching** — per-residue quenching rates and contact radii. Editing a row
   changes the chemistry for that amino acid only.
5. **FRET** — enable it, place the acceptor, and give R₀ **in Ångström**.

## What comes out
Quantum yield and mean lifetime, the donor (and FRET) decay, the dye
trajectory, and its autocorrelation.

Everything in this form is one QuEst *project*. **Save project** writes exactly
the JSON the command line (`quest simulate project.json`) and the web UI read,
so a run started here can be finished anywhere.

ui.web.tour.welcome.title: Welcome to QuEst
ui.web.tour.welcome.body: This short tour walks you through the whole workflow: loading a protein, placing a dye, running and reading a simulation, scanning residues and tuning the advanced settings. Use the arrow keys or the buttons to move on.
ui.web.tour.step1.title: Workflow tabs
ui.web.tour.step1.body: Work through the stages left to right: Labeling, Simulation, Scan and Advanced Settings. The active stage is highlighted and drives which settings the sidebar shows.
ui.web.tour.step2.title: Load a structure
ui.web.tour.step2.body: Type a four-letter PDB ID and press Load, or upload your own PDB/CIF file. QuEst resolves chains, residues and atoms from it.
ui.web.tour.step3.title: Upload a file
ui.web.tour.step3.body: Prefer a local file over a PDB ID? Upload a PDB or CIF here; the structure replaces the loaded one and the labeling selects repopulate.
ui.web.tour.step4.title: Simulation runs
ui.web.tour.step4.body: Every simulation is saved. Pick a previous run here to reload its labeling site, parameters and results.
ui.web.tour.step5.title: Structure panel
ui.web.tour.step5.body: Confirms what is loaded: the filename plus chain and atom counts. Nothing will run until this shows a structure.
ui.web.tour.step6.title: Place the dye
ui.web.tour.step6.body: Pick the chain, residue and atom the dye attaches to. A dye cannot be tethered to the waters or ions at the end of the structure.
ui.web.tour.step7.title: FRET acceptor
ui.web.tour.step7.body: Optionally add a second dye and define an acceptor site. The Forster-based energy transfer is then combined with the PET quenching in the decay.
ui.web.tour.step8.title: Accessible volume
ui.web.tour.step8.body: Defines the space the linker lets the dye explore around the attachment atom. The linker length is the value the simulation uses.
ui.web.tour.step9.title: Structure viewer
ui.web.tour.step9.body: This 3D view draws the structure and the labelling site. It updates as you change the chain, residue and atom selects.
ui.web.tour.step10.title: Run the simulation
ui.web.tour.step10.body: Once a structure is loaded, hit Run Sim. The decay, quenching and dye trajectory appear on the Simulation tab.
ui.web.tour.step11.title: Simulation settings
ui.web.tour.step11.body: Lifetime, viscosity and the other model parameters live here on the Simulation tab. The value next to each field is what the current run used.
ui.web.tour.step12.title: Simulation results
ui.web.tour.step12.body: The Simulation tab reads the decays, the quenching-rate histograms and the dye trajectory for the focused site and its acceptors.
ui.web.tour.step13.title: Scan settings
ui.web.tour.step13.body: Choose which residues to evaluate — a single site or every residue in the chain — before running the batch scan.
ui.web.tour.step14.title: Scan results
ui.web.tour.step14.body: The scan table reports lifetime, quantum yield, contact fraction and the accessible/contact volumes per residue. Columns sort and filter, and the results export to the clipboard.
ui.web.tour.step15.title: Quenching parameters
ui.web.tour.step15.body: Under Advanced Settings you can edit the per-residue quenching rates that drive the PET model.
ui.web.tour.step16.title: Simulation configuration
ui.web.tour.step16.body: The settings that shape how a simulation is computed — confirmations and advanced model switches live here.
ui.web.tour.step17.title: Dye stickiness
ui.web.tour.step17.body: Dyes slow down inside the protein, not just at it; the slowing radius captures that transient and is a run parameter you can return to.
ui.web.tour.step18.title: JSON mode
ui.web.tour.step18.body: Flip Configuration to JSON Mode to edit the raw project object instead of the curated form. Both drive the same state.
ui.web.tour.step19.title: Save a preset
ui.web.tour.step19.body: Save the current parameters as a named dye preset you can bring back with the Dye selector, instead of re-typing values.
ui.web.tour.step20.title: Language
ui.web.tour.step20.body: Switch the whole interface — labels, help text and this tour — between English, German and French. Your choice is remembered.
ui.web.tour.step21.title: Theme
ui.web.tour.step21.body: Toggle between the light and dark appearance. The theme is saved for next visit.
ui.web.tour.step22.title: Cite QuEst
ui.web.tour.step22.body: Click here to see exactly how to cite QuEst in a paper.
ui.web.tour.step23.title: Download
ui.web.tour.step23.body: Finally, download the results of the current run as a file, or Clear to reset the application and start again.
ui.web.tour.done.title: All set
ui.web.tour.done.body: That is the full workflow: load a structure, place a dye, run a simulation, scan residues and fine-tune the model. You can reopen this tour any time from the button at the top.
